correctness.rationale: For a positive Perron vector w of K, the empty-state Jacobian obeys J(c)w=(cρ(K)−1)diag(m)w. Irreducible Metzler bounds give the asserted stability sign on either side of 1/ρ(K). Conjugation by diag(sqrt(q_i d_i)) yields the symmetric weights sqrt(q_i q_j/(d_i d_j)). Because the inserted edge was absent, no old edge has both endpoint degrees changed. Each old weight is multiplied by 1 or sqrt(d/(d+1))≥1/sqrt(2). The new positive edge improves the Rayleigh quotient strictly on the old positive Perron vector. For q=(1,b,1), the transpose reduced to the invariant (end,center) subspace has characteristic polynomials x²−b before and x²−x/2−b/2 after insertion, and symmetry places the Perron vector in this subspace. This recovers R(b)=(b^{-1/2}+sqrt(8+b^{-1}))/4. It is strictly decreasing, with the stated endpoint limits; equivalently each R>1/sqrt(2) is realized by b=(2R−1/R)^{-2}. Equality is impossible for any allowed instance, and two or fewer vertices cannot furnish a missing edge in a connected simple graph. Thus the reciprocal critical-rate factor is always strictly below sqrt(2). Independent symbolic reduction and combinatorial counts 81+6,804+763,020=769,905 for the stated finite grid are replayable via python /workspace/branches/independent_checks.py. The numerical grid minimum was not needed for the theorem and was not independently recomputed.
